focused_validation.scope: Capture maintenance, capture erasure/retention, all ambient unit cases, shared privacy authority and erasure coordinator

worktree_review_failures.cause: Existing fixture teardown assumed real cleanup finished inside a deliberately tiny 10 ms observation budget, before new background I/O had drained
worktree_review_failures.correction: Keep the 10 ms observation budget and explicit timeout/lease assertions unchanged, and await actual retained close tasks before ExitStack closes fixture databases

causes: Concurrent active-store and maintenance connections could both attempt the same schema ALTER
The initial test helper returned while a follow-up sweep had just been scheduled after a clock/location change
corrections: Serialize schema and column inspection/ALTER in BEGIN IMMEDIATE with rollback and ready state after commit
Wait actual currently scheduled sweep scopes to quiesce; retain shielded work if the observer times out
Anchor due time to the receipt computation timestamp so late harvest never adds another delay

ownership.schema_ownership: BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes migrations across connections; failed initialization rolls back and does not publish ready state
ownership.close_order: stop scheduling, actual archive reservation/encoding/discard calls, retained scheduler and sweeps, peer database closure, actual disk operations/executor, privacy ledger and writer lease

proven: The capture factory starts independent maintenance before ambient producers and without enabling ambient, keep_audio or semantic recall
Expired SQLite text, conversation scopes and unattached FLAC locators are removed at startup and on new earlier deadlines without a running transcriber or an erasure request
Persisted per-row and intent deadlines survive reads and restarts; a shorter configured cap is honored without extending an earlier stored deadline
Known historical databases and roots remain included after location changes; active stores share registry roots, file guards and the owned disk scope

Two bounded database sweeps and a dedicated two-thread disk executor allow another independent target to finish while one unlink or database fails; saturating the default executor does not starve retention
Live or unverifiable references in registered databases sharing an archive root prevent unlink; checks read only metadata and never peer transcript/speaker content
Shared legacy numeric rowids protect files even before attachment; expired numeric legacy orphans are durably queued in batches with a strict scandir traversal
Missing databases/directories are not created, orphaned data without an attributable database remains unavailable, and corrupt or unsupported targets do not become false successful cleanup
Failed unlink survives restart with a durable pending count; status exposes only opaque target IDs, counters and fixed error codes
Cancelling scheduler observers leaves actual sweeps and native operations owned; a close timeout retains the writer lease until those operations actually finish
Archive ownership now spans reservation, native encode and discard rather than ending when only the encoder returns
Concurrent initialization of three store connections over five fresh databases completes with one copy of every migration column
A late scheduler harvest uses the original receipt timestamp; moving the test clock to expiry does not postpone the due sweep again
An independent Python process rejects imports of Torch, Chroma, sentence-transformers, faster-whisper and ONNX Runtime while disabled capture retention initializes, sweeps and closes successfully

The source-free CPython 3.13 smoke writes a real synthetic FLAC, advances the injected privacy clock, runs independent TTL cleanup with ambient/recall disabled, and verifies physical cleanup without a conversation tombstone
limits_and_remaining: H3 remains incomplete: capture and semantic-index conversation-erasure drivers are connected, while producers, contexts, events, diagnostics, collectors, streams, suggestions and voices remain unregistered; no broad erasure endpoint or completion promise is exposed
The registry tracks known locations and must still be reconciled with the private real-data inventory; it cannot discover paths never registered
Unattributable files without databases, unknown file protocols, unsupported target versions and unavailable shared references remain pending for review; no source or capture date is invented
Legacy numeric-orphan cleanup retains the prior mtime rule; new UUID clips rely on durable pre-encoder intents. Unknown legacy data still needs the copy migration/inventory rehearsal before release

A non-cooperative native write, locked SQLite database or unavailable filesystem can delay physical cleanup; read-time expiry/revocation remains enforced and actual work stays owned rather than being reported erased
STT, audio readers, tap buffers and active distillation batches still require producer/reader erasure coordination
Independent physical index reconciliation of all TTL expiry and individual fact deletion while recall is disabled remains pending
Structured logs, JSONL/Logstash metrics, collectors, live events/frontend queues, suggestions and alternate prompt consumers still require source/retention policy
Ambient pause, total mute with non-audio reactivation, acoustic fingerprint/group retention, manual voice review and calibrated evaluation remain pending
The real 870-record legacy-copy migration and compatible restore rehearsal remain pending; restore must preserve tombstones and durable cleanup intent
H0/H1 real HA effects, H2 physical capture/audio/barge-in, H4 recovery, H5 remaining voice functions and H6 integrated runtime/GC/hardware/release/rollback acceptance remain open
